blocking_findings.rule: Condition URNs name a textual variant. They belong to the text and carry no edition (JLPTEI-3 'condition URNs'; 'a variant belongs to the text rather than to any one edition'). SIDDUR_URN_SCHEME: 'A URN names a text. It does not name a book… or a position'; 'changes of placement and differences of edition do not justify new identities'. For an occurrence that differs only in pointing or punctuation, the documented mechanism is that the 'repeated occurrence may carry its… URN in tei:seg/@source… preserving the printed occurrence without creating a duplicate canonical corresp mapping'. These selectors are named by printing position, embed language codes (/he/, /en/) and source_fragment_N, and gate differences that are almost entirely maqaf, punctuation, plene spelling and meteg.
blocking_findings.note: The Areshet conclusion selectors (first_printing/zikhronot_printing) were already accepted; this batch extends that pattern to retzeh, modim, modim_derabbanan, vekhol_hachayyim and hayom_harat_olam.

blocking_findings.rule: (a) The URN is described as the existing full Shacharit identity. If the Shacharit repetition file in the same project already maps it, this milestone is a second identical @corresp. refdb keeps only the first and warns (DuplicateUrnError per SIDDUR_URN_SCHEME). 'Do not duplicate a canonical URN merely because the text is printed again'. The scheme says identical text is transcluded. (b) Every @source points at prayer:amidah/birkat_kohanim_leshatz, the shorter Birnbaum extent this batch decided not to use. That makes a false quotation claim. (c) A new Shacharit-path identity is registered in a Musaf batch, and nothing reviewed here emits it. (d) The Musaf-specific rubric 'הש״ץ בקול' sits inside the canonical scope.

NAMING_SCHEME: a path component may not contain '-', which marks a range. Registry URNs name texts, not ranges. Neither URN is emitted by any XML in this PDF294–311 batch. The first is a garbled range expression, and the second is an unrelated Minchah unit.

Neither URN is in registry-additions. identity-search shows that no corpus file realizes them. It also shows the same project already realizes these words as siddur:rosh_hashanah/musaf/shofarot_close and …/shofarot_close/text (musaf_shofarot_close.xml). 'One text has exactly one URN across every work containing it.' As it stands, the silent and repetition printings of the same berakhah have unrelated identities, and the new ones may be unregistered (urn_registry --check cross-checks every prayer: URN emitted).

blocking_findings.rule: JLPTEI-3 'Kinds of rubric': a rubric that says what the passage is, who says it, or how is a description. One that says both when and what is also a description. SIDDUR_URN_SCHEME: 'Speaker labels… are emitted as tei:note type="description" carrying the URN in @corresp' (role/reader, role/congregation). Elsewhere in this batch, ק׳/ח׳/קו״ח are encoded this way, so these notes are inconsistent with the batch's own practice.

SIDDUR_URN_SCHEME poem: 'Stanzas without a canonical numbering are addressed by transliterated incipit'. 'Name by incipit, not by ordinal… Never number it.' JLPTEI-3 gives the same rule (yonah_matzah/hayom). There are 90 new registrations, and they are cheap to rename now but frozen after acceptance and 1.0.

nonblocking_findings: N1 Contextual chapter URNs end in components that are not chapters: <tei:milestone unit="chapter" n="19" corresp="…/quotes/exodus_19/occurrence_19"/> and <tei:milestone unit="chapter" n="9" corresp="…/quotes/zechariah_9/partial_15"/>, each nested under another chapter URN (files 10, 11, 33, 34). The scopes do terminate correctly. For Zechariah, chapter 9 is closed and immediately reopened with nothing in between. Keep one quotes/zechariah_9 scope across verses 14 and 15. The verse-part (adonai_tzevaot_yagen) already marks the partial extent, so the partial_15 layer is redundant. For Exodus 19:19 use a sibling occurrence name rather than nesting.

N2 Liturgical words are held under siddur: URNs: …/shofarot_verses/intro_* ('כַּכָּתוּב בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ', 'וְנֶאֱמַר') and the …/quotes/* contexts. SIDDUR_URN_SCHEME says siddur: 'holds no words of its own', and the Birnbaum composite-verse extension is scoped to Hodu–Ashrei. The Shofarot verse paragraph is also said in the silent Musaf. Check for, and reuse, any identity the silent printing already has.

N3 Unused registrations: …/areshet_zikhron_words, …/ken_tagen_words, …/modim_derabbanan_english_words, …/avodah_word_parts and …/hodaah_word_parts. The word-host files (12, 14, 17, 18, 20, 25, 35, 37, 40, 41, 42) emit no div @corresp and no idno for them. Remove them or emit them.

N4 Registry records lack parent/kind. Labels are mechanical ('stanza 1', 'intro exodus 19 16', '16', 'partial 15'), the ken_tagen label_en is a transliteration, and every note is the same boilerplate. The intermediate nodes (poem:anusah_leezrah/exodus_19_16, …/quotes, siddur:…/shofarot_verses/quotes, …/shofarot_close/quotes) are not registered, which may fail the registry parentage check.

N5 ken_tagen_weekday and ken_tagen_shabbat are two siddur: units with identical content on the same leaf (n305/n306). If the book prints Ken tagen once, use one unit after both conditionals, as the expanded spine does. Otherwise it prints twice when Shabbat is undefined.

N6 The ed second token 'rosh_hashanah/musaf/repetition/anusah_leezrah' is not a registered siddur: unit, and anusah is printed only once. SIDDUR_URN_SCHEME reserves the second token for a second printing of the same text, named by its siddur path. Parallel streams on shared pages need a documented convention.
N8 Abbreviations are inconsistent: הש״ץ, ע״ס and א״ב are left unexpanded, while ק׳, ח׳, קו״ח and נ״א are given tei:choice/abbr/expan.
N9 shofarot_calls (07) contains an empty <tei:p> </tei:p>, and its unit holds only a directive.

N10 Whitespace inside j:option: ' תְּקִיעָתֵנוּ…' (20) and ' our Teruah.' / ' our Tekiah.' / ' our Tekioth.' (42), plus the double space in 'לְקוֹל  ' and 'sound of  ' that ends areshet_sefatenu/opening.
N11 The English avodah host (40) has biblScope for p.18 only, although Musaf p.144 transcludes it. The scheme asks for one biblScope per printing.
N12 Every occurrence file declares both the he and en variant features, so each language's file declares the other language's features. Harmless noise.
N13 Bare stanza terminators appear between adjacent stanzas. Adjacent units already share a boundary, so these are redundant but harmless.

N14 The expanded spine adds editorial bilingual rubrics with resp=codex. These are acceptable as editorial, but confirm they are gated or styled as editorial and do not count as filled-in translation.

Header events (lines 1–55) were not read for most files, and lines 56–88 were not read for 24, 26, 27, 28, 31, 36 and 43. The headers I did read (00, 01, 02, 12, 29 in full, and lines 56–88 of most others) were identical boilerplate.
The expanded spine tail closes #section_musaf_repetition_s220_settings, whose j:declare opens outside the excerpt, so I could not verify the sibling constraint.
No scan images were viewed. Human source readings were taken as given, and the draft editionStmt was not treated as a defect.
The schema run was not available to me. This review does not rely on schema validity.
verdict: NOT APPROVED. The Areshet zikhron hosting, Veteerav reuse, generic Ken tagen identity, facs mapping and sic/corr handling follow the guidelines. Seven blocking issues remain: wording selectors keyed to printing position and language that gate punctuation-only differences; Musaf reuse of the Shacharit Birkat Kohanim identity that likely duplicates a mapping and points @source at the rejected Birnbaum extent; malformed and out-of-scope registry records; unverified new Shofarot-close identities alongside an existing project identity for the same text; speaker labels and source notes typed as instructions; ordinal stanza URNs where the scheme requires incipits; and a duplicate p.137 page break.
